standard.title: Repeated chance experiments
standard.description: Conduct repeated chance experiments to observe relationships between outcomes; identify and describe the variation in results
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can conduct repeated chance experiments, record results and discuss variation (AC9M3P02). They have not yet investigated the relationship between theoretical likelihood and experimental outcomes across a larger number of trials, or connected chance experiments to AI applications.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students conduct repeated chance experiments, record and order outcomes, and identify and describe variation in results.

nodes.label: Plan and conduct chance experiments
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can select a chance device, conduct a repeated experiment and record outcomes systematically.
nodes.minimum_width: Conduct a chance experiment at least 10 times using one device (coin, dice or spinner); record outcomes in a table.
nodes.typical_width: Conduct repeated experiments using coins, dice, spinners and card draws; record outcomes systematically; use both physical and virtual random generators; connect to the idea that AI systems use random generators to train algorithms.
wider: Investigate two simultaneous coins — recording outcomes systematically (HH, HT, TH, TT) and comparing observed frequencies after many trials
Conduct the same experiment using a physical device and a virtual one, comparing the distributions and discussing whether the digital tool produces 'random' results in the same way
success_criteria: Students can conduct a repeated chance experiment at least 10 times and record outcomes in an organised format
Students can identify all the possible outcomes for their experiment

nodes.label: Identify and describe variation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can describe variation in experimental results and discuss what causes it.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify variation in results across repeated trials; describe one pattern or departure from an expected pattern.
nodes.typical_width: Compare results across multiple repetitions of the same experiment; identify and describe variation; discuss why results vary (chance); compare results with predictions; discuss how results change as the number of trials increases.
wider: Play strategic games (Noughts and Crosses, First to 20) and investigate whether the order of play affects the chance of winning — distinguishing games of pure chance from games with strategic elements
Pool class results from the same experiment to produce a combined dataset, comparing individual variation with the combined distribution and discussing what changes with more trials

response_modes.reason: Students often expect experimental results to exactly match the theoretical probability (e.g. exactly 5 heads in 10 tosses). Encountering variation across multiple independent trials — and pooling class results to see the distribution stabilise — builds understanding of probability as a long-run tendency.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Pooling class results and watching a distribution stabilise as trials increase is a genuinely surprising and memorable demonstration of how probability works. This is one of the richest pedagogical moments available in primary probability.
success_criteria: Students can describe the variation in their experimental results
Students can explain that variation is expected in chance experiments and is not an error
